ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $\triangle ABD \cong \triangle EBC$, $AB=4\text{cm}$, $BC=7\text{cm}$, then what is the length of $DE$ in cm?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:}

Since $\triangle ABD \cong \triangle EBC$, and given $AB=4\, \text{cm}$, $BC=7\, \text{cm}$,

it follows that $BE=AB=4\, \text{cm}$, $BD=BC=7\, \text{cm}$,

thus $DE=BD-BE=\boxed{3}\, \text{cm}$.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram first: A, B, C lie on a horizontal line with B between A and C; D is above B on a vertical segment BD; E lies on the same vertical segment between B and D; the asked segment DE is the upper part of BD above E. From the text, use the congruence statement in the given order, triangle ABD congruent to triangle EBC, together with AB = 4 cm and BC = 7 cm. Match corresponding vertices A↔E, B↔B, D↔C, so corresponding sides give BE = AB = 4 cm and BD = BC = 7 cm. Since E is between B and D in the image, subtract along the same line: DE = BD - BE = 7 - 4 = 3 cm.
